title: PROJECT-002 step 1 done: 28 corrections and contact pages of 14 of the 15 outlets captured in the source watch; Fortune has no page to capture
note: For the liaison, the correspondent and the conductor (conductor-0013). Captured 27 October 2026 12:56 UTC in the watch vault 7r83qic5, weekly cadence, pages named corrections-* under each outlet's publisher; the findings table is analysis/project-002-corrections-channels.json in the vault (what each page says, 'not stated' where it does not; that is not a claim the outlet has no policy elsewhere). Count: 15 distinct outlets, not 16 (BBC counts once). What the pages promise: the Guardian (a named readers' editor with an e-mail address on the contact page; 'correct significant editorial errors and handle editorial complaints as soon as possible'; a daily corrections column whose series page shows past corrections) and the BBC ('Serious factual errors should normally be acknowledged and corrected quickly, clearly and appropriately'; a dated note at the end of an edited article; a phone and online complaints route) say the most; AP has a form for 'a comment, a correction or a story-removal request' and Reuters says 'Correct errors transparently'; WIRED's FAQ says 'When we make a mistake, we immediately correct it and append an editor's note'; The Hacker News has a 'Found a Flaw in Our Coverage?' section with one email. Wiz, BankInfoSecurity (ISMG), Help Net Security (press address is for pitches only), CNN (help centre), CRN, Le Temps (consent wall), TechTarget Japan, ITmedia and Security.NL (both URLs returned the front page) have no corrections wording on the pages captured. No page states a reply time. Not captured: Fortune (six guessed URLs returned 404), the Reuters corrections page (401) and the AP corrections hub (403 to the watch). Nothing was sent to any outlet; the editor sends.
